content.comment_body: When I attempt to download an [product_name] project to the [product_name] device, I consistently receive a "Download Failed! Invalid project" message. This happens even with a simple test project that only has a rectangle. What could be causing this? Are there specific access control settings I need to check? - The diagnostic indicates the SD card is fine - Deploying to SD card works

I'm experiencing the same issue, using a newer version of [product_name], specifically [version_no]. It seems the project is corrupted. Why this happens isn't clear to me. I recommend contacting [company_name] directly and submitting a support request.
Since deploying to SD card works, I'll use that for now. However, it's inconvenient to remove the SD card every time the project needs updating.
It seems this may just be how things currently work. Still, this shouldn't be considered normal operation. I strongly suggest starting a support request.

There is no /img/ subdirectory in your corrupted project archive. [product_name] typically creates this folder when setting up a new project. You may have deleted it unintentionally. Try creating a new project, then copy the /img/ directory and its contents from the new project into your problematic project folder. Afterwards, reopen your broken project and attempt to load it onto the controller. $ ls ~/NetBeansProjects/Broken_p1/img/ Default.png loading.gif pb_go.png pb_stop.png uibg2.png uibg5.png
The question remains: Why didn't [product_name] generate this subdirectory? A user reported having the same issue even with a newly created empty project.

This suggests the [product_name] installation itself is corrupt. Templates for new projects are stored in a directory like <[product_name]_Install_Dir>/lwe/res/web/edit/ When a new project is created, this directory's contents are copied over. If the /img/ folder is missing or renamed here, the project can still be edited but cannot be downloaded to the [product_name] device.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering problems downloading projects from [product_name] to [product_name] devices, with an error marking the project as invalid. The issue affects projects of all complexities and points to missing or corrupt files within either the project folder or the installation itself. Users have proposed workarounds such as manually copying missing directories from a new project or using SD card deployment, but these solutions are cumbersome and reveal underlying reliability issues in [product_name]'s project creation and installation integrity.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth project downloads directly from [product_name] to the device, without errors or manual fixes. The [product_name] installation should reliably include all necessary template files for project functionality.
